comparison: Perfect agreement on morphological differences (C1-C4). Both evaluations find these claims well-supported by the 3D reconstructions and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the careful characterization.

Perfect agreement on synaptic connection findings (C5-C7). Both evaluations support the claims about similar latencies despite longer distances. Peer reviewers treat this as a key discovery of the study.

Perfect agreement on axonal propagation speed (C8). Both evaluations accept the finding of no significant species difference in axonal conduction velocity, confirming compensation occurs in dendrites rather than axons.

Strong agreement on dendritic propagation speed differences (C9, C10, C65, C66). Both evaluations affirm this as the central mechanistic finding with convincing evidence. OpenEval includes C11 (correlation) while peer review addresses it separately in R5.

Partial overlap on C11 (correlation between forward and backward propagation). OpenEval groups this with C9-C10 findings, while peer review treats it as separate supporting evidence. Both accept the correlation as valid.

Strong agreement on electrophysiological properties (C12-C13). Both evaluations accept these characterizations. Peer review also includes C14 in this grouping, while OpenEval addresses C14 separately in R6.
Partial overlap on HCN channel experiments. OpenEval covers C14-C18, peer review covers C12-C14. Both accept the pharmacological evidence ruling out HCN channels as the primary mechanism.
Strong agreement on HCN channel pharmacology (C15-C18). Both evaluations accept this evidence as carefully tested and ruling out one potential mechanism for species differences.

Perfect agreement on active conductance experiments (C19-C20). Both evaluations accept the pharmacological evidence showing these channels contribute to propagation but don't fully explain species differences.

Perfect agreement on membrane capacitance and thickness (C21-C23). Both evaluations accept these measurements and the inference that these factors don't explain species differences, helping narrow down the mechanism.

Strong agreement on dendritic diameter findings (C24-C25). Both evaluations affirm this as a key mechanism. Peer review also includes C67 in this grouping, connecting diameter to the broader conclusion.

Strong agreement on computational modeling validation (C26-C28). Both evaluations support the modeling approach. Peer review also includes C37-C38 in this grouping, while OpenEval addresses those separately in R13.

Strong agreement on basal tree area and hybrid cell experiments (C29-C33). Both evaluations affirm this as central mechanistic insight. Peer review also includes C45 in this grouping, while OpenEval addresses C45 in R15.

Strong agreement on fitted cable parameters (C34-C36). Both evaluations accept the parameter fitting and the finding of similar membrane time constants. Peer review also includes C68 in this grouping.

Strong agreement on modeling with fitted parameters (C37-C38). Both evaluations accept this validation of species differences. Peer review groups these claims with the broader modeling results (C26-C28).
Perfect agreement on factor importance ranking (C39-C41). Both evaluations accept the systematic analysis using GLM and SHAP methods as comprehensive and well-validated.

Strong agreement on compensatory mechanisms and functional implications (C42-C45). Both evaluations accept the integrated conclusions about preserved timing and coincidence detection. Peer review also includes C46-C47 in this grouping.
Strong agreement on preserved coincidence detection (C46-C47). Both evaluations accept this functional implication. OpenEval treats this separately while peer review groups it with C42-C45.

Perfect agreement on evolutionary conservation interpretation (C48-C52). Both evaluations affirm that biophysical properties are adapted to maintain information transfer speed despite morphological scaling.

Perfect agreement on STDP and plasticity implications (C53-C57). Both evaluations accept the functional interpretation connecting faster bAP propagation to shifted STDP rules and the cited supporting literature.

Perfect agreement on fast oscillations and memory context (C58-C62). Both evaluations accept this broader functional interpretation and the connection to circuit-level functions supported by cited literature.
OpenEval addresses sample characteristics (C63-C64) and notes potential age confounding. Peer reviewers do not explicitly evaluate these descriptive claims about the experimental samples.
Partial overlap on integrated conclusions. OpenEval covers C67-C69, peer R10 includes C67 with diameter findings. Both support the conclusion about thicker dendrites as a mechanism.
Partial overlap on integrated conclusions. OpenEval covers C67-C69, peer R13 includes C68 with cable parameters. Both support the conclusion about compensatory passive properties.

Significant disagreement on C69 (passive vs. active properties). OpenEval finds this claim supported, but peer Reviewer 2 expresses uncertainty, noting 'the contribution of active membrane properties cannot be excluded' and that further investigation is needed.
